introduction: A cluster has its own versions, certificates, storage and recovery needs. An upgrade changes that operating system of components, not merely a kubectl binary. Check supported skew, removed APIs and workload compatibility before deciding the order.

This is the permitted component-focused alternative to completing every Hard Way step. Compare two verified kind patch images in separate disposable clusters, exercise a bounded worker failure, and write the supported upgrade sequence for your chosen real distribution. kind replacement is not an in-place production upgrade, and the evidence must say so.
prerequisites: Earlier kind/kubectl lessons and Docker with Linux containers. Confirm kind version and kubectl version --client.
The tested devopps-taskboard:local image exists. Enough local capacity for one control-plane/worker cluster; run candidates sequentially if necessary.
Week 45 trust map and explicit distinction between etcd state and application data.

concepts.title: Version compatibility is a matrix
paragraphs: Check API server, kubelet, proxy, controllers, client and webhooks separately. Current policy keeps kubelets no newer than the API server, bounds skew and prohibits skipping API-server minor versions. Distribution tools may impose narrower requirements.

The two pinned 1.35 patch images below were verified to exist. They are bounded teaching artifacts, not a recommendation to run an early patch in production. Select the latest supported patch after your distribution/release review.
concepts.example: A webhook can reject new API behavior even while every node is Ready.
concepts.judgment: A version matrix is necessary but cannot prove data safety or spare capacity during maintenance.

concepts.title: Maintenance and backup protect different things
paragraphs: Cordon prevents new scheduling; drain evicts eligible workloads subject to disruption rules. A PodDisruptionBudget can correctly stop maintenance when the proposed change breaks its availability promise.
etcd stores Kubernetes objects. It does not contain all PostgreSQL volume bytes or external bucket data. Restoring a PVC object can restore a reference to a missing disk.
concepts.example: Do not use forced drain to hide a capacity problem.
concepts.judgment: Existing traffic may continue briefly during control-plane failure while new scheduling and reconciliation stop; test both paths.

steps.title: 1 · Create an isolated component lab
steps.purpose: Explicit cluster names and contexts protect earlier course environments.

commands.code:
cd ~/dev-opps-lab
mkdir -p evidence/week-46
kind version
kubectl version --client
cat > evidence/week-46/kind.yaml <<'YAML'
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
nodes:
- role: control-plane
- role: worker
YAML
kind create cluster --name devopps-internals --image kindest/node:v1.35.0@sha256:4613778f3cfcd10e615029370f5786704559103cf27bef934597ba562b269661 --config evidence/week-46/kind.yaml
kubectl --context kind-devopps-internals get nodes -o wide
explain: The literal YAML requests one control-plane and worker. The registry digest selects exact node bytes.
Every kubectl call supplies --context, avoiding a global default switch. -o wide records actual versions and placement.
commands.expected: Two Ready nodes in the new named cluster.
commands.troubleshoot: If your kind version is incompatible, update it using the earlier reviewed setup procedure and record the mismatch. Never target another cluster to get a green result.

steps.checkpoint: Capture API/client/node versions before changing anything.

steps.title: 2 · Exercise a bounded maintenance decision
steps.purpose: Observe disruption controls without bypassing them.

commands.code:
kubectl --context kind-devopps-internals get pods -A -o wide
kubectl --context kind-devopps-internals cordon devopps-internals-worker
kubectl --context kind-devopps-internals drain devopps-internals-worker --ignore-daemonsets --timeout=60s
kubectl --context kind-devopps-internals uncordon devopps-internals-worker
explain: get records placement. cordon blocks new scheduling. drain evicts eligible Pods, ignores node-following DaemonSets and has a 60 second deadline.
No --force or local-data-deletion bypass is provided. Inspect a blocking Pod/PDB instead of removing safeguards. uncordon permits scheduling again.
commands.expected: Worker returns Ready and schedulable; any blocked drain is recorded with its real cause.
commands.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

steps.checkpoint: Explain which application data is absent from an etcd-only backup.

steps.title: 3 · Compare a patched replacement
steps.purpose: Validate a user operation on the candidate rather than checking node health alone.

commands.code:
kind create cluster --name devopps-internals-next --image kindest/node:v1.35.1@sha256:05d7bcdefbda08b4e038f644c4df690cdac3fba8b06f8289f30e10026720a1ab --config evidence/week-46/kind.yaml
kubectl --context kind-devopps-internals-next get nodes -o wide
kubectl --context kind-devopps-internals-next get --raw=/readyz
kind load docker-image devopps-taskboard:local --name devopps-internals-next
kubectl --context kind-devopps-internals-next create deployment taskboard-probe --image=devopps-taskboard:local -- python -m uvicorn reference.stage03:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --no-access-log
kubectl --context kind-devopps-internals-next rollout status deployment/taskboard-probe --timeout=90s
kubectl --context kind-devopps-internals-next port-forward deployment/taskboard-probe 8101:8000
explain: The second cluster uses the verified next patch. API readiness and node readiness are separate checks.

kind load supplies the local image. The deployment overrides the default stage 07 command with a deliberately memory-only probe; it tests the platform boundary without claiming persistent data migration.
rollout has a deadline. port-forward remains running in this terminal and binds locally by default.
commands.troubleshoot: If capacity prevents two clusters, record/delete the first only after preserving evidence, then create the candidate.

commands.code:
cd ~/dev-opps-lab/app/taskboard
source .venv/bin/activate
curl --retry 10 --retry-delay 1 --retry-connrefused --max-time 5 -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8101/livez
TASKBOARD_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8101 TASKBOARD_TEST_MODE=memory python -m pytest tests/system -q
explain: Use a second terminal. Memory mode explicitly skips identity isolation; tests reach the candidate listener through forwarding.
The bounded read-only liveness wait confirms the forwarded memory server is accepting requests before tests start.
commands.expected: Memory HTTP contract passes; persistence/auth migration remain separate checks.
commands.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

steps.checkpoint: Write keep/replace/abort reasoning and label replacement versus in-place evidence.

failure.title: A worker agent stops reporting
failure.boundary: Only kubelet inside the explicitly named disposable kind worker.

inject.code: docker exec devopps-internals-worker systemctl stop kubelet
explain: Stop the agent inside this lab container, never a host production worker.
inject.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

explain: Watch node conditions; heartbeat/grace periods mean NotReady is not instantaneous. Ctrl+C stops the watch only.
investigate.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

investigate.code: docker exec devopps-internals-worker systemctl status kubelet --no-pager
explain: Read the specific component state without opening a pager.
investigate.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

hints: The API may remain healthy when one agent fails.

explanation: The stopped kubelet removes node reconciliation and heartbeats. Restore it and wait for actual node readiness. API health alone never proved worker health.

recover.code: docker exec devopps-internals-worker systemctl start kubelet
explain: Restore only the deliberately stopped service.
recover.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

explain: Bound the recovery observation and investigate if it expires.

questions.prompt: What is missing from an etcd snapshot?
questions.answer: Application volume contents and external stores are separate. etcd holds Kubernetes descriptions and references.

questions.prompt: Why not force a blocked drain?
questions.hint: What promise is the blocking condition protecting?
questions.answer: A PDB or local-data constraint may protect availability/data. Add capacity or revise the plan deliberately.

questions.prompt: What upgrade did this exercise prove?
questions.answer: A pinned patch replacement runs the tested stateless workload. It does not prove in-place distribution upgrades or persistent-data migration.

exercise.brief: Write the real distribution upgrade runbook while preserving this component lab evidence boundary.
constraints: Choose exact current/target versions and current policy.
No minor skipping; supported control-plane-before-worker sequence.
deliverables: Version matrix, prechecks, drain/backup plan, postchecks and recovery decision.
Candidate workload result and component failure timeline.
hints: Webhooks and removed APIs can fail despite Ready nodes.
solution: Verify backups, update one supported bounded scope through distribution tooling, test business operations and stop on declared regressions.
Do not turn replacement success into a claim of in-place upgrade safety.

cleanup.code:
kind delete cluster --name devopps-internals-next
kind delete cluster --name devopps-internals
explain: Stop port-forward withCtrl+C first; delete only these two disposable clusters.
cleanup.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

repoConnections.principle: Context is part of every cluster operation
repoConnections.application: A kubeconfig identifies clusters, users and contexts. Convenient switching makes target verification essential. Use a restricted lab identity, inspect events and logs, then reproduce findings with kubectl. Connect symptoms to the correct resources in the intended cluster rather than memorizing a GUI path. Practice: Inspect the bad-image drill with one dashboard, record context and namespace, then reproduce image and event evidence with kubectl.

repoConnections.principle: Follow identity through the control plane
repoConnections.application: The API server accepts requests; controllers reconcile; the scheduler chooses nodes; kubelet runs assigned workloads; etcd stores control-plane state. Certificates and kubeconfigs connect responsibilities to identities. Manual setup exposes these boundaries. A small single-control-plane exercise does not establish resilient production design. Practice: Draw the request and identity path for Pod creation. Explain each component credential and observe one controlled fault in the bounded internals lab.

repoConnections.principle: An extension creates an operating obligation
repoConnections.application: Add-ons introduce APIs, privileges, configuration and upgrade dependencies. State the missing capability, maintainer, failure behavior and removal plan before installing. Shortlist using primary docs and supported versions. A local function test is separate from resilience and upgrade evidence. Practice: For one add-on, record purpose, permissions, compatibility, failure signal, rollback and removal. Reject it if existing components already satisfy the requirement.

notes: Commands and configurations are supplied for the stated disposable lab. Authoring host has no operational Docker/WSL; container, database and cluster exercises are not claimed executed. Record your own outputs before passing a gate.
